analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only. cli-reference.md changes the date (line 3) and adds a `--prompt-prep` benchmark row (head line 572). Units :10 and :11 are unchanged surrounding context (lines 1337-1807), and I saw nothing there that alters security behavior. The only substantive change is the new "Prompt preparation and admission" table in configuration.md (head 587-596). It documents five env vars: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _PROMPT_CACHE_MB, _PROMPT_CACHE_VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. All are described as forwarded by LaunchAgent.

No code is in this batch, so these claims are unverified: PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift, ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift and LaunchAgent passthrough. For the next pass:
- The prompt token cache is described as scoped to the request's prefix-cache scope (coordinator-authored from account, model build and prompt contract). This is in-memory per tokenizer, with a 32 MiB default and a 4096 MiB max. It adds a second hit/miss timing signal on tokenization. This is adjacent to T-041/SEC-035 (TTFT oracle, same-account only). If the scope were not enforced, it would be a cross-tenant channel. Also check whether it persists prompt-derived data, whether it is purged with KEK wipe or unload, and whether the 4096 MiB cap permits memory-pressure DoS (TB-007).
- DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE lets later coordinator events overtake a request waiting for model load. This touches ordering around cancel, grant and revocation handling (T-053, T-010) and needs a check that stale authorization is not used.
- The documented fail-closed behavior (a verify mismatch or a throwing uncached path disables reuse) is a mitigation to confirm in code.
- The doc states the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 disable also turns the prompt cache off, which is consistent with the T-041 kill switch.

No concrete regression is shown by the supplied evidence, so there are no findings. Because the code is outside the evidence, the cache-scoping and timing questions remain open, and the T-041 threat model may need a note about the new tokenization-cache timing channel once code is reviewed.
